Lower eyelid blepharoplasty, commonly referred to as under eye bag removal surgery, is a popular procedure for individuals seeking to rejuvenate their appearance by addressing under-eye bags, puffiness, and sagging skin. These concerns, often caused by aging, genetics, or lifestyle factors, can make you look tired or older than you feel. At AestheticEye in Cincinnati, OH, our board-certified surgeons, Dr. Ginger Henson and Dr. Jonathan Pargament, specialize in lower eyelid surgery to help you achieve a refreshed and youthful look.

Blepahroplasty Quiz

What is Lower Blepharoplasty?

Lower blepharoplasty is a surgical procedure designed to correct issues with the lower eyelids. This surgery targets and removes excess fat, skin, and sometimes muscle from the lower eyelids, resulting in a smoother and more even appearance. Lower blepharoplasty effectively eliminates under-eye bags and puffiness, giving you a more alert and rejuvenated look.

Benefits of Lower Eyelid Surgery

Choosing lower eyelid surgery at AestheticEye offers numerous benefits, including:

Elimination of Under-Eye Bags

This procedure targets and removes the excess fat and skin that cause under-eye bags, resulting in a smoother and more even appearance.

Reduction of Puffiness

By addressing the underlying causes of puffiness, lower eyelid surgery provides a more rested and alert look.

Smoothing of Wrinkles and Fine Lines

The surgery can also help to minimize the appearance of wrinkles and fine lines around the lower eyelids.

Enhanced Self-Confidence

Achieving a more youthful and refreshed appearance can boost your self-esteem and confidence.

The Under Eye Bag Removal Procedure

At AestheticEye, our surgeons utilize advanced techniques to ensure the best possible outcomes for lower blepharoplasty. During the procedure, an incision is made either just below the lower lash line or inside the lower eyelid (transconjunctival approach). Through this incision, excess fat, skin, and sometimes muscle are removed or repositioned to create a smoother contour. The incision is then carefully closed, resulting in minimal scarring that is typically well-hidden.

Recovery and Results of Lower Blepharoplasty

View More Before & After Results

Recovery from lower eyelid surgery is generally smooth, with most patients experiencing mild swelling and bruising for the first week or two. Cold compresses and prescribed medications can help manage these symptoms. Most patients return to their normal activities within 10-14 days. The final results, which can be seen as swelling subsides, include a more youthful and rejuvenated appearance with diminished under-eye bags and puffiness.

Frequently Asked Questions | Under Eye Bag Removal — Lower Blepharoplasty

Are There Non-Surgical Options to Treat Under Eye Bags?

Yes, non-surgical options such as chemical peels and dermal injectables can temporarily reduce the appearance of under-eye bags and wrinkles. However, these treatments do not provide the same long-lasting results as surgical procedures.

Is Under Eye Bag Removal Covered by Insurance?

Under eye bag removal is typically considered a cosmetic procedure and is not covered by insurance. However, if the surgery is performed to improve vision or address a medical condition, insurance may cover some or all of the costs.

What Is Recovery Like After Lower Blepharoplasty?

Recovery involves mild swelling and bruising for the first week or two. Patients can use cold compresses and prescribed medications to manage discomfort. Most return to normal activities within 10-14 days.

How Soon Will I See Results from Lower Eyelid Surgery?

Initial results are visible as swelling and bruising subside, typically within two weeks. The final results, showing a smoother and more youthful under-eye area, will be evident within a few months.

How Long Does Lower Eyelid Surgery Take?

Lower eyelid surgery usually takes between one to two hours, depending on the complexity of the procedure and the individual patient’s needs.

Can I Get Under Eye Bag Surgery After PRK or LASIK Surgery?

Yes, you can undergo lower eyelid surgery after PRK or LASIK surgery. However, it is important to wait until your eyes have fully healed from the previous procedures. Our surgeons will evaluate your individual case to determine the appropriate timing for surgery.
